A1.s: You meet your new neighbour in the morning.
o: Good morning! Nice to meet you.
Good night! Nice to meet you.
Morning. Who are you?
n: 'Good night' is for going to bed.
Sounds rude to a new person.

A1.s: You want a coffee. The waiter looks at you.
o: A coffee, please.
Give me coffee.
Coffee me, please.

A1.s: You want to know the price of a T-shirt.
o: How much is this, please?
How many is this?
Price. Tell me.

A1.s: You arrive at the hotel. You have a booking.
o: Hello, I have a reservation.
Hello, I am a reservation.
Give me my room.

A1.s: Your teacher says something, but you don't understand.
o: Sorry, can you repeat that?
What? Again!
Sorry, can you repeat me?

A1.s: A friend says, 'How are you?'
o: I'm fine, thanks. And you?
I have fine.
Why do you ask?

A1.s: You are lost. You want the train station.
o: Excuse me, where is the station?
Where is station? Tell.
Hey you, station where?
n: Rude and not a full sentence.

A1.s: You finished your meal. You want to pay.
o: Can I have the bill, please?
Bring money paper.
I pay now. Go.

A1.s: You call a friend. Someone else answers.
o: Hi, is Anna there, please?
Who are you?
Give phone to Anna.
n: A rude way to start a call.
Too direct, and words are missing.

A1.s: The assistant asks, 'Can I help you?' You are just looking.
o: No, thanks. I'm just looking.
No. Go away.
I am only see.

A1.s: At check-in, the worker asks for your passport.
o: Sure, here you are.
Take.
Yes, here you go are.

A1.s: You want some water with your lunch.
o: Can I have some water, please?
Water. Now.
Can I have some waters, please?

A1.s: You arrive late to class.
o: Sorry I'm late.
I am late, so what?
Sorry for my late.

A1.s: It's your friend's birthday today.
o: Happy birthday!
Happy birthday day!
Good birthday to you.

A1.s: You need the Wi-Fi password at the hotel.
o: What's the Wi-Fi password, please?
Wi-Fi password. Give.
How is the Wi-Fi password?

A1.s: You want to know if this bus goes to the centre.
o: Does this bus go to the centre?
This bus go centre?
Bus! Centre! Yes?

A1.s: You walk into someone by accident.
o: Oh, sorry!
Watch out!
Oh, excuse!

A1.s: The waiter asks, 'Ready to order?' You need more time.
o: Not yet, sorry. One minute, please.
No. Go.
I am not ready for order you.

A1.s: You can't find the milk in the supermarket.
o: Excuse me, where's the milk?
Where you put milk?
Milk is where, please?
n: Sounds like blame, and grammar errors.

A1.s: It's your first day. You meet a new colleague.
o: Hi, I'm Sam. I'm new here.
Hi, my name Sam. I new.
Who is the boss?

A1.s: You call a restaurant to book a table for two.
o: Can I book a table for two?
Table. Two people. Tonight.
Can I book two tables for me?
n: Wrong meaning: you need one table.

A1.s: You are leaving a party.
o: Bye! See you soon.
Hello! See you soon.
I go. Bye bye forever.

A1.s: The doctor asks, 'What's the problem?' Your head hurts.
o: I have a headache.
My head is hurt me.
Head. Bad.

A1.s: You get in a taxi. You want to go to the airport.
o: The airport, please.
Drive airport fast.
I go to airport, please?

A1.s: You want a croissant, and you want to take it away.
o: One croissant to take away, please.
One croissant to take out from here.
Croissant. Bag.

A1.s: You lost your room key.
o: Sorry, I lost my room key.
Key is lost. Fix.
Sorry, I losed my key.

A1.s: You want to know the time. You ask a stranger.
o: Excuse me, what time is it?
Excuse me, what hour is it?
Time? Quick.

A1.s: You need to borrow a pen from a classmate.
o: Can I borrow a pen, please?
Can I lend your pen?
Pen. Give me.

A1.s: You want to pay by card.
o: Can I pay by card?
Can I pay with card of me?
Card. OK?

A1.s: A friend gives you a small present.
o: Thank you so much!
Why? What do you want?
Thank you very many!

A1.s: You can't find your gate at the airport.
o: Excuse me, where is gate 12?
Where gate 12 is?
Gate 12! Where?!
n: Wrong word order in a question.

A1.s: You want to see the menu.
o: Can I see the menu, please?
Can I watch the menu?
Menu, quick.

A1.s: You call someone, but it's the wrong number.
o: Oh, sorry. Wrong number.
Who are you? Bye.
Sorry, I have a wrong phone.

A1.s: Your colleague says, 'Have a nice weekend!'
o: Thanks, you too!
Thanks, me too!
Why?

A1.s: You want to change dollars to euros.
o: Hi, can I change money here?
Hi, can I change monies here?
Money. Change it.

A1.s: The receptionist asks your name.
o: My name is Ali Khan.
I am calling Ali Khan.
Why you need my name?

A1.s: A woman has a cute dog. You want to say something nice.
o: What a lovely dog!
What a lovely dog have you!
Your dog is very fat.

A1.s: You want to know what time breakfast starts.
o: What time is breakfast?
When breakfast is?
Breakfast time, tell me.

A1.s: You want to try on a jacket.
o: Can I try this on, please?
Can I test this jacket on me?
I wear this now.

A1.s: Your friend asks, 'Pizza or pasta?' You want pizza.
o: Pizza, please!
Pizza is me.
I don't care. Whatever.
n: Sounds rude, and you want pizza.

A2.s: The shirt is too small. You want a bigger one.
o: Do you have this in a larger size?
This is small. Bring other.
Do you have this in more big?

A2.s: You are allergic to nuts. You want to order a cake.
o: Does this cake have nuts in it?
Is there nuts or no?
I hope no nuts. Bring cake.

A2.s: You call the dentist to make an appointment.
o: Hi, I'd like to make an appointment, please.
Hi, I want to do an appointment.
Give me a time tomorrow.

A2.s: You will be late for work because the bus is late.
o: Hi, sorry, my bus is late. I'll be there soon.
The bus is late. Not my problem.
Sorry, I will be late because bus late.

A2.s: Your hotel room is very cold.
o: Excuse me, my room is very cold. Can you help?
My room is freezing. Fix it now.
Excuse me, my room has cold.

A2.s: A friend invites you to the cinema, but you're busy.
o: Sorry, I can't tonight. Maybe next time?
No. I don't want.
Sorry, I am not possible tonight.
n: Polite, and keeps the door open.

A2.s: A tourist asks you for directions. You don't know the way.
o: Sorry, I'm not from here.
I don't know. Use your phone.
Sorry, I am not knowing.

A2.s: Your coffee is cold.
o: Sorry, my coffee's a bit cold. Could you warm it up?
This coffee is terrible. Again.
Excuse me, can you make my coffee more hot?

A2.s: The doctor asks how long you've had a cough.
o: For about three days.
Since three days.
Long time. I don't count.
n: Use 'for' with a period of time.

A2.s: You missed class yesterday. You want to know about homework.
o: Sorry, I was absent yesterday. Was there any homework?
Give me the homework from yesterday.
Sorry, I was missing yesterday. Is homework?
n: Not natural. Say 'Was there any homework?'

A2.s: You want to return a broken lamp. You have the receipt.
o: Hi, I'd like to return this. It's broken.
This lamp is rubbish. Money back.
Hi, I want to give back this broken.

A2.s: Your neighbour's music is loud at midnight.
o: Hi, sorry, could you turn the music down a bit?
Stop the music! People are sleeping!
Hi, can you make the music more small?

A2.s: You want a window seat on the plane.
o: Could I have a window seat, please?
I sit at window. OK?
Can I have a seat of window?

A2.s: A colleague offers you a coffee. You don't want one.
o: No, thanks. I'm fine.
No. The coffee here is horrible.
No, I don't want, thanks.

A2.s: You and a friend want to pay for your meals separately.
o: Could we pay separately, please?
We pay two times, please.
Separate! Each one pays!

A2.s: The line is bad. You can't hear the person.
o: Sorry, you're breaking up. Can you say that again?
What? Speak better!
Sorry, I can't listen to you.

A2.s: You want to open a bank account.
o: Hi, I'd like to open an account, please.
Hi, I want to make open an account.
Account. I need one now.

A2.s: Your friend passed her driving test.
o: Congratulations! That's great news!
Finally! It took you forever.
Congratulation for your pass!

A2.s: You want to leave your bags after checking out.
o: Could I leave my bags here until 3?
I leave bags here. Bye.
Can I let my bags here until 3?

A2.s: The cashier gave you the wrong change.
o: Sorry, I think this is the wrong change.
You stole my money!
Sorry, the change is not correctly.

A2.s: The pharmacist gives you medicine. You don't know when to take it.
o: How often should I take this?
How many times I take this?
Medicine when? Tell me.

A2.s: You want a stranger to take a photo of you and your friend.
o: Excuse me, could you take a photo of us?
Excuse me, can you make a photo to us?
Hey, take photo. Quick.

A2.s: You need one more day to finish your homework.
o: Could I have one more day for my homework, please?
I didn't do it. Tomorrow.
Can you give me more days for do homework?

A2.s: The barista calls the wrong name, but it's your drink.
o: I think that's mine. It's Sara, not Tara.
That's wrong! Can't you write?
This is my, but the name is bad.

A2.s: Your manager asks you to finish a report today. You can.
o: Sure, no problem. I'll send it this afternoon.
Fine. If I must.
Sure, I finish it in the afternoon.

A2.s: Your neighbour took in a parcel for you.
o: Thanks so much for taking my parcel!
Why did you take my parcel?
Thanks for take my parcel!

A2.s: The taxi driver is going too fast. You feel scared.
o: Could you slow down a little, please?
Slow down! Are you crazy?
Could you drive more slowly little?

A2.s: There's a hair in your food.
o: Excuse me, there's a hair in my food.
Disgusting! I'm not paying!
Excuse me, there is hair in the my food.

A2.s: You're at a friend's home. You need the toilet.
o: Can I use your bathroom?
Where do you do toilet?
I need toilet. Now.

A2.s: Passport control asks, 'What's the purpose of your visit?'
o: I'm here on holiday.
I'm here for holiday make.
Why do you want to know?

A2.s: An old man needs a seat on the bus.
o: Please, have my seat.
Sit here if you want, old man.
Please, take my sit.

A2.s: Someone calls for your colleague, but she isn't here.
o: Sorry, she's not here right now. Can I take a message?
She's not here. Call later. Bye.
Sorry, she's out. Can I leave a message?
n: You 'take' a message; the caller 'leaves' one.

A2.s: You want to check out of the hotel later than usual.
o: Would it be possible to check out a bit later?
I check out late tomorrow.
Can I check out more late?

A2.s: You're buying a gift. You want it wrapped.
o: Could you gift-wrap this, please?
Make it pretty for me.
Could you pack it like present?

A2.s: You are sick. You call your boss in the morning.
o: Hi, I'm not feeling well, so I can't come in today.
I'm sick. Bye.
Hi, I am illness today, so I don't come.

A2.s: Your friend tells you her cat died.
o: Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that.
It's only a cat. Get a new one.
Oh no, I'm so sorry for hear that.

A2.s: The doctor's advice is not clear to you.
o: Sorry, could you explain that again?
That makes no sense.
Sorry, can you explain me again?

A2.s: The cash machine kept your card.
o: Hi, the cash machine kept my card. Can you help?
Your machine ate my card! Terrible!
Hi, the machine eated my card.

A2.s: Someone's bike is blocking your front door.
o: Excuse me, is this your bike? It's blocking my door.
Move your bike! Now!
Excuse me, your bike is closing my door.

A2.s: You don't understand why you got a low mark.
o: Could you explain why I got this mark?
This mark is wrong. Change it.
Why you give me this bad mark?

B1.s: Your flight is delayed. You ask a staff member for information.
o: Excuse me, do you know how long the delay will be?
Why is everything always late here?
Excuse me, how long will be the delay?

B1.s: You booked a double room, but they give you a single.
o: Sorry, I think there's a mistake. I booked a double room.
You gave me the wrong room. Typical.
Sorry, I reserved a room for double.

B1.s: You meet a friend you haven't seen for months.
o: Hey! It's been ages! How have you been?
Hey! You look much older.
Hey! Long time no seeing! How you are?

B1.s: A new colleague looks lost in the office kitchen.
o: Hi, are you looking for something? I can help.
You're new, right? Don't touch my milk.
Hi, what are you searching? I help you.

B1.s: You've waited 40 minutes and your food still hasn't come.
o: Excuse me, we ordered quite a while ago. Will our food be long?
This is ridiculous. Where's our food?
Excuse me, we are waiting since 40 minutes.
n: Too angry for a first complaint.

B1.s: Someone gives you directions, but they speak too fast.
o: Sorry, could you say that a bit more slowly?
Stop! You talk too fast.
Sorry, could you speak more slow?

B1.s: You call a hotel to ask if they have rooms this weekend.
o: Hi, do you have any rooms available this weekend?
Rooms this weekend? How much? Quickly.
Hi, is there some rooms available for this weekend?

B1.s: The shoes you bought last week are already broken.
o: Hi, I bought these last week and they've already broken.
These shoes are garbage. I want my money.
Hi, I bought these last week and since they broke.

B1.s: The taxi driver seems to take a much longer route.
o: Sorry, isn't it quicker to go along the main road?
You're cheating me. Stop the car.
I think you go the long way on purpose.
n: A polite question, not an accusation.

B1.s: The receptionist says the next appointment is in two weeks.
o: Is there anything sooner? It's quite urgent.
Two weeks? I could die by then!
Is there something more early? It's urgent.

B1.s: A new family moves in next door.
o: Hi, I'm Tom from number 12. Welcome to the street!
Hi. Please don't be noisy like the last people.
Hi, I'm Tom. Welcome in the street!

B1.s: A colleague asks for help, but you're very busy.
o: I'd love to help, but I'm swamped. Could we do it later?
Not my job. Ask someone else.
I would like help, but I am very busy now.

B1.s: A friend cooked you dinner. You didn't like it much.
o: Thanks for dinner! It was really kind of you.
Honestly, it wasn't very good.
Thanks! The food was a very interesting taste.

B1.s: Your suitcase didn't arrive after the flight.
o: Hi, my suitcase didn't arrive. Where can I report it?
You lost my bag! I want compensation now!
Hi, my suitcase didn't come out. Who I tell?

B1.s: A classmate keeps talking while you're trying to study.
o: Sorry, would you mind keeping it down? I'm trying to focus.
Shut up, please.
Sorry, would you mind to be quiet?

B1.s: There's a payment on your account you don't recognise.
o: Hi, there's a payment here I don't recognise. Could you check it?
Someone stole my money. It's your fault.
Hi, there is a payment that I don't know him.

B1.s: The room next to yours is very noisy at night.
o: Hi, the room next door is really noisy. Could you do something?
I can't sleep! Throw them out!
Hi, the next room is making many noises.

B1.s: You missed a call from a friend. You call back.
o: Hi, sorry I missed your call. What's up?
Why did you call me?
Hi, sorry I lost your call.

B1.s: The café is full. You see an empty chair at a stranger's table.
o: Excuse me, is anyone sitting here?
I'm sitting here. OK?
Excuse me, is this place busy?

B1.s: You forgot your friend's birthday yesterday.
o: I'm so sorry I forgot your birthday! Let me buy you lunch.
Birthdays aren't important anyway.
Sorry, I forgot your birthday. It happens.
n: Apologises and makes up for it.

B1.s: Someone pushes in front of you in the queue.
o: Excuse me, I think I was next.
Hey! Back of the queue, idiot!
Excuse me, I was here first before you.

B1.s: Your manager asks if you can work on Saturday. You can't.
o: I'm afraid I can't this Saturday. I already have plans.
No way. Weekends are mine.
I'm afraid I can't. I have plan.
n: A polite refusal with a reason.

B1.s: A stranger at the bus stop says, 'Terrible weather, isn't it?'
o: I know! I hope it clears up soon.
It's just rain. Relax.
Yes, the weather is very terrible.

B1.s: You can't choose a dish. You ask the waiter for help.
o: What would you recommend?
What's not disgusting here?
What do you recommend me to eat?
n: Not natural. Just 'What do you recommend?'

B1.s: Someone is sitting in your reserved seat on the train.
o: Sorry, I think this might be my seat. Is it 24B?
Get up. That's my seat.
Sorry, I think you are in my place reserved.

B1.s: You want to know if a new medicine has side effects.
o: Are there any side effects I should know about?
Will this medicine kill me?
Is there side effects?

B1.s: A friend invites you to a party. You'd like to bring a friend.
o: Sounds fun! Is it OK if I bring a friend?
I'll come, but only if it's a good party.
Sounds fun! Can I bring with me a friend?
n: Word order: 'bring a friend with me'.

B1.s: You don't want your hotel room cleaned today.
o: Could you skip my room today, please? It's fine as it is.
Don't come in my room.
Please don't make my room today.

B1.s: Your laptop stops working just before a meeting.
o: Sorry, my laptop's just crashed. Could I borrow yours for a minute?
My laptop died. Give me yours.
Sorry, my laptop is broken. Can you lend me your?

B1.s: You might miss your next flight. The security queue is long.
o: Excuse me, my flight leaves in 30 minutes. Could I go ahead?
Move! I'm missing my flight!
Excuse me, my flight goes in 30 minutes. Let me pass first.

B1.s: You don't understand the grammar the teacher explained.
o: Sorry, could you give another example? I'm not sure I got it.
That explanation was confusing.
Sorry, I don't understand. Can you explain more easy?

B1.s: Leaves from your neighbour's tree keep falling into your garden.
o: Would you mind trimming your tree? The leaves fall into our garden.
Your tree is a problem. Cut it.
Hi, can you cut your tree because it is making leaves?

B1.s: You were on hold for 20 minutes. Finally, someone answers.
o: Hi, thanks for picking up. I'm calling about my internet.
Finally! Twenty minutes! Unbelievable!
Hi, I call because of my internet is not working.
n: Polite, and gets to the point.

B1.s: A friend still hasn't paid back the money you lent them.
o: Hey, just a quick reminder about the money from last month.
Where's my money? You always forget.
Hey, you must give me back my money now.

B1.s: The price on the shelf is lower than at the till.
o: Sorry, the shelf said €5. Could you check it?
You're trying to trick me.
Sorry, on the shelf it was writing €5.

B1.s: The waiter asks, 'How is everything?' Your steak is overcooked.
o: It's nice, but the steak's a bit overcooked, actually.
Terrible. The steak is like a shoe.
It's fine, but the steak is cooked too much time.

B1.s: A driver almost hits you on the crossing.
o: Hey, careful! That was close.
Learn to drive, you idiot!
Hey, be careful! You almost crashed me.

B1.s: You want to know if breakfast is included.
o: Is breakfast included in the price?
Breakfast is free, yes?
Is breakfast inclusive the price?

B1.s: Your colleague just got a promotion.
o: Congratulations! You really deserve it.
Wow, I'm surprised they chose you.
Congratulations for your promote!

B1.s: Your train is cancelled. You ask about the next one.
o: Excuse me, when's the next train to Leeds?
Your trains never work. When's the next one?
Excuse me, when comes the next train to Leeds?
n: Word order: 'when does the next train come'.

B2.s: A colleague suggests an idea you think won't work.
o: I see your point, but I'm not sure it'll work with our budget.
That's a bad idea.
I am agree with you, but it will not work.

B2.s: Your manager hasn't answered your request from Monday.
o: Just following up on my email from Monday. Any update?
Why haven't you answered my email yet?
I remember you about my email from Monday.

B2.s: The bill includes a dessert you didn't order.
o: Sorry, I think there's a mistake. We didn't have the dessert.
You're overcharging us on purpose.
Sorry, but you charged us something we didn't eat it.

B2.s: A colleague keeps interrupting you in meetings.
o: Sorry, could I just finish my point?
Stop interrupting me all the time!
Wait, I am not finished to speak.

B2.s: Your online order arrived damaged. You call customer service.
o: Hi, my order arrived damaged. I'd like a replacement, please.
Your delivery people are useless.
Hi, my order arrived damaging. I want a change.
n: Clear, and says what you want.

B2.s: A friend shares an opinion you strongly disagree with.
o: Hmm, I actually see it a bit differently.
That's the stupidest thing I've heard.
I disagree you completely.

B2.s: Your hotel room looks nothing like the photos online.
o: The room's quite different from the photos. Is there another one available?
This is false advertising. I'll sue you.
The room doesn't look like the photos. Change me the room.
n: Calm, and asks for a solution.
Not natural. Say 'Could I change rooms?'

B2.s: A salesperson calls you. You're not interested.
o: Thanks, but I'm not interested. Have a good day.
Don't ever call me again!
Thanks, but I don't have interest for this.

B2.s: Your manager gives you a task with an impossible deadline.
o: I'll do my best, but realistically I'll need until Thursday.
That's impossible. Forget it.
OK, no problem, it'll be done today.
n: Honest, and offers a realistic date.

B2.s: You didn't understand a point your boss made.
o: Sorry, could you clarify what you meant by 'phase two'?
That made no sense at all.
Sorry, could you clear what you meant?

B2.s: Your neighbour often parks in your parking space.
o: Hi, would you mind not parking in my space? I need it in the mornings.
If you park there again, I'll call the police.
Hi, please stop to park in my place.

B2.s: You're writing to a company for the first time.
o: Dear Sir or Madam, I'm writing to enquire about your courses.
Hey guys, quick question about your courses.
Dear Sir or Madam, I write you for asking about courses.
n: Too casual for a first email.

B2.s: The bank charged you a fee you think is unfair.
o: Could you explain this fee? I wasn't told about it.
Give me my money back or I'm leaving this bank.
Could you explain me this fee? Nobody said me.
n: Say 'explain it to me' and 'told me'.

B2.s: A friend always arrives late when you meet.
o: It'd be great if you could let me know when you're running late.
You're always late. It's so selfish.
Please come in time next times.

B2.s: The doctor prescribes antibiotics. You're not sure they're necessary.
o: Could I ask why antibiotics are needed in this case?
I don't trust antibiotics. No.
Why you give me antibiotics? Is it necessary?

B2.s: The shop won't give a refund without a receipt.
o: I understand, but could you offer store credit instead?
That's a stupid rule.
I understand, but can you make an exception for one time?

B2.s: A colleague's mistake has affected your work.
o: I noticed a couple of issues in the figures. Could we go through them?
You messed up my work again.
There are mistakes from you in the numbers.
n: Focuses on the problem, not the person.

B2.s: You want to add an idea after a colleague finishes speaking.
o: Can I just add something to that?
No, here's what we should actually do.
Can I add to this one thing?
n: A polite way to join in.

B2.s: The airline overbooked your flight and offers you a later one.
o: I understand. What compensation can you offer for the delay?
This is your problem, not mine. Put me on this flight.
I understand. What can you give me for compensate?
n: Calm, and asks about your rights.

B2.s: A friend asks your opinion on a jacket you don't like.
o: It's not really my style, but if you love it, go for it!
It's ugly. Don't buy it.
It doesn't suit to you, I think.

B2.s: You must tell a client their delivery will be late.
o: Unfortunately, there's been a delay. Your order should arrive by Friday.
Your order is late. Sorry, not our fault.
Unfortunately, your order will arrive with delay of three days.

B2.s: You arrive early. Your room is still being cleaned.
o: That's fine. Could I leave my bags and come back later?
Seriously? I paid for a clean room now.
That's fine. Can I leave my bags and come back more late?

B2.s: Your manager asks for your honest opinion on a new plan.
o: Overall I like it, but I have a few concerns about the timeline.
Honestly? It's a disaster.
I like it, but I have some worries for the timeline.
n: Too harsh, and gives no detail.

B2.s: The customer service agent can't solve your problem.
o: I appreciate your help. Could I speak to a supervisor, please?
You're useless. Get me your boss.
Thanks. Could I talk with your chief?

B2.s: The meeting is running late and you have another one.
o: Sorry, I've got another meeting at three. Could we wrap up soon?
I'm leaving. This is taking forever.
Sorry, I must go because I have other meeting.

B2.s: You booked a quiet table, but they seat you by the kitchen.
o: We did ask for a quiet table. Is there anything else available?
This is the worst table. Unacceptable.
We asked a quiet table. Is there other?

B2.s: Your neighbour does loud building work early every Sunday.
o: I know you're renovating, but could you avoid early Sunday mornings?
Some of us want to sleep, you know.
Could you please make your works less early on Sundays?

B2.s: You want to ask your manager for a pay rise.
o: Could we discuss my salary? I've taken on a lot more recently.
I want more money or I'll quit.
Could we discuss about my salary?

B2.s: Your friends plan a trip you can't afford.
o: It sounds amazing, but it's a bit out of my budget this time.
That's way too expensive. Who has that money?
It sounds amazing, but my pocket is not enough.

B2.s: You sent a client the wrong file by mistake.
o: Apologies, I attached the wrong file. Please find the correct one attached.
Oops, wrong file lol. Here.
Sorry, I have attached wrong file. Here is the right.

B2.s: You've waited an hour past your appointment time.
o: Sorry to bother you. Do you know how much longer it'll be?
I've been here an hour. This is a joke.
Sorry, how much time still I must wait?

B2.s: The salesperson pushes an expensive warranty you don't want.
o: Thanks, but I'll pass on the warranty.
Stop trying to sell me things.
Thanks, but I don't need warranty, no.

B2.s: Two colleagues are arguing. You want to calm things down.
o: You both make valid points. Maybe we could find a middle ground?
You're both wrong. Stop arguing.
Both of you have reason. Let's find a middle.
n: Literal. Say 'you both have a point'.

B2.s: A colleague asks you to cover their shift again.
o: I covered last time, so I'm afraid I can't this time.
No. You always do this.
I did it last time, so this time I don't can.

B2.s: The hotel charged you twice for the same night.
o: I think I've been charged twice for Tuesday. Could you check?
You double-charged me. Are you trying to steal?
I think you charged me two times the same night.

B2.s: A friend asks why you didn't come to their party.
o: I'm really sorry. Something came up at the last minute.
I just didn't feel like it.
Sorry, something came up on the last minute.

B2.s: A colleague often sends you urgent work late on Fridays.
o: Could you send things by Thursday where possible? It helps me plan.
Stop sending me work on Fridays. It's annoying.
Please send the works before Friday for my planning.

B2.s: Your loan application was rejected. You want to know why.
o: Could you tell me what the main reasons for the decision were?
Why did you reject me? It's unfair.
Could you tell me what were the reasons?

B2.s: A colleague presents your idea as their own.
o: I'm glad you liked the idea I shared. Shall we develop it together?
That's my idea. You stole it.
That was my idea. Why you took it?

B2.s: Your internet provider promised a fix, but nothing happened.
o: I was told this would be fixed by Monday. What's the next step?
You people never keep your promises.
I was told it would be fixed until Monday.

C1.s: You must tell a team member their work isn't good enough yet.
o: There are some strong points here, but a few areas need more work. Shall we go through them?
This isn't good enough. Redo it.
Your work is quite bad, but don't worry about it.

C1.s: You're politely declining a job offer.
o: Thank you for the offer. After careful consideration, I've decided to accept another position.
Thanks, but I got something better.
Thank you. Unfortunately I must refuse your offer because I don't want it.
n: A blunt reason, it sounds rude.

C1.s: Your boss's plan has a serious flaw. Everyone else is silent.
o: Could I raise one concern? I'm worried the timeline might not leave room for testing.
This plan won't work, and everyone here knows it.
With all respect, your plan is simply wrong.

C1.s: At a business lunch, your guest's card is declined.
o: Please, let me get this one. You can get the next.
Oh dear, your card doesn't work?
Your card has been refused. Do you have another way to pay?

C1.s: A friend asks if you like her new partner. You have doubts.
o: I don't know him well yet, but if he makes you happy, that's what matters.
Honestly, I think he's bad for you.
He seems nice, I suppose, if you like that type.

C1.s: A client calls, angry about an error your company made.
o: I completely understand your frustration, and I'm sorry. Let me sort this out right away.
Please calm down. Shouting won't help.
These things happen sometimes. It's not a big deal.

C1.s: Your neighbour's dog barks all day while she's out.
o: I wondered if you knew Max barks quite a lot while you're out? He might be lonely.
Your dog is driving everyone crazy.
Excuse me, your dog makes a big noise always.

C1.s: You're the hotel manager. A guest's room isn't ready yet.
o: I'm terribly sorry, your room isn't quite ready. May I offer you a drink while you wait?
Your room isn't ready. Come back later.
Sorry, the room is not ready yet, but it's not our fault.
n: Defensive; the guest doesn't care whose fault.

C1.s: You need to chase a senior client for an overdue payment.
o: I'm writing regarding invoice 214, which appears to be outstanding. Could you look into it?
You still haven't paid. Please pay immediately.
Hey, did you forget to pay us, by any chance?
n: Too blunt for a senior client.
Too casual for a formal matter.

C1.s: In a negotiation, the other side's offer is far too low.
o: I appreciate the offer, but it's quite a way off what we had in mind.
That's insulting. Try again.
OK, fine, we accept. No problem.

C1.s: You have to tell your team about upcoming budget cuts.
o: I'll be honest: we're facing some cuts, but I'll keep you informed at every step.
Bad news: there's no money. Deal with it.
Don't worry, nothing will change for anyone.

C1.s: A friend practises his wedding speech for you. It's far too long.
o: It's lovely! Maybe trim it a little so the best stories really stand out.
It's way too long. People will get bored.
It's perfect, don't change a thing!

C1.s: As a doctor, you must tell a patient their results need more checks.
o: The results show something we'd like to look at more closely. It's a precaution.
Something's wrong. We need more tests.
Don't worry, it's probably nothing, but maybe it's something.

C1.s: As a teacher, you tell a parent their child is struggling with maths.
o: Emma's a lovely student. She's finding maths tricky, so let's work on it together.
Your daughter is bad at maths.
Emma is a lovely student, but her maths is a disaster.
n: A positive start, then a plan.

C1.s: As a bank adviser, you have to reject a customer's loan.
o: I'm afraid we're unable to approve it at this stage, but let's look at other options.
Rejected. Your credit score is too low.
Sadly, the computer said no, so nothing can be done.

C1.s: As the manager, you must refuse a refund that's against policy.
o: I understand your disappointment. While I can't refund it, I can offer an exchange.
Rules are rules. No refund.
Sorry, it's impossible. Please understand me.

C1.s: A senior colleague shows wrong figures in front of a client.
o: Just to add, I believe the latest figure is 12%. I'll double-check afterwards.
Those numbers are wrong.
Sorry, but you're making a big mistake there.
n: Too blunt in front of a client.

C1.s: You're replying to a colleague's angry and unfair email.
o: Thanks for your email. I think there may be a misunderstanding; could we discuss it by phone?
How dare you write to me like that?
I am not agree with anything in your email.
n: Calm, and moves it off email.

C1.s: A friend has been staying with you for weeks. You need your space back.
o: It's been lovely having you, but I'll need my space back soon. How are your plans looking?
You need to leave. This is too much.
So, when are you finally going home?

C1.s: Your manager offers you a project you really don't want.
o: Thanks for thinking of me. I'd like to focus on the launch right now, though. Could someone else take it?
No thanks, it sounds boring.
Thank you, but I prefer not to do it. It's not interesting.

C1.s: You must cancel a meeting with an important client at short notice.
o: I'm so sorry for the short notice, but I'll have to reschedule. Would Thursday suit you?
Can't make it today. Another time.
Sorry, the meeting is cancelled. I'm busy.
n: Apologises and offers a new date.

C1.s: At a work dinner, your host offers you wine. You don't drink.
o: That's very kind, but I'll stick to water tonight, thanks.
I don't drink. Alcohol is bad for you.
No. Take it away, please.

C1.s: A neighbour wants to cut down a tree you love.
o: I can see why the shade bothers you. Could we look at trimming it instead?
Absolutely not. It's my tree.
OK, do what you want with it.
n: Gives up something you care about.

C1.s: As the manager, you see a VIP guest complaining loudly in the lobby.
o: I'm so sorry about this. Shall we step into my office so I can help properly?
Please lower your voice. There are other guests here.
Calm down, sir. It's not so bad.
n: Calm, and moves it somewhere private.

C1.s: You must tell your boss you'll miss an important deadline.
o: I wanted to flag early that we're behind. I can deliver by Monday; would that work?
We won't make it. Sorry.
The deadline was unrealistic from the start, so we'll miss it.
n: An early warning plus a solution.

C1.s: In a formal email, you need to decline a supplier's proposal.
o: Thank you for your proposal. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite meet our needs at present.
Not interested. Thanks anyway.
Hi! Thanks, but nah, it's not really for us.

C1.s: One person keeps talking, and others can't get a word in.
o: Great points. I'd love to hear what others think too. Sara?
Can you let someone else talk for once?
OK, enough. Next person.

C1.s: A friend asks to borrow a large sum of money. You'd rather not.
o: I'm really sorry, but I have a rule about not lending money to friends. Can I help another way?
No way. You'd never pay it back.
Sorry, I am not in the position for lend money.

C1.s: You think the doctor misunderstood where your pain is.
o: Sorry, I may not have been clear. The pain is actually on the left side.
You're not listening. I said left.
You understood wrong, it's on the left.

C1.s: You're a cashier. An elderly customer is slow to pay and the queue is restless.
o: Take your time. Would you like a hand with the card machine?
Hurry up, please, people are waiting.
Can someone help her? She's too slow.

C1.s: A new colleague's joke upset someone on the team.
o: Have you got a minute? I think that joke may have landed badly with a few people.
That was offensive. Apologise to everyone now.
Haha, OK, but maybe don't, you know?

C1.s: A friend calls while you're busy at work.
o: Hey! I'm just in the middle of something. Can I call you back in an hour?
I'm busy. Bye.
Sorry, now is not good moment for me.

C1.s: You're writing to your company's CEO for the first time.
o: Dear Ms Patel, I hope you're well. I'm writing to propose a new idea.
Hi Sarah! Hope you're good! Quick idea for you.
Dear Madam CEO, I am writing for proposing a new idea.

C1.s: You need to disagree with a client's choice of design.
o: I can see the appeal. Could I show you an alternative that might suit your audience better?
With respect, that design is ugly.
As you wish. It's your money.

C1.s: You must tell an employee they didn't get the promotion.
o: It was a tough decision. You weren't selected this time, but I'd like to plan your next step together.
Sorry, they picked someone better.
You didn't get it. Maybe next year.

C1.s: A friend proudly shows you a painting that isn't very good.
o: I love the colours you've used! How long did it take?
Did a child paint this?
It's... interesting. Maybe painting isn't your thing.

C1.s: As the manager, you must refuse a guest's request for a free upgrade.
o: I'm afraid we're fully booked tonight, but I'd be happy to note it for your next stay.
No free upgrades. Sorry.
Unfortunately this is not possible, you must pay for upgrade.

C1.s: Your boss interrupts your presentation with a wrong assumption.
o: That's a good question. I'll actually be covering that on the next slide, if that's OK.
You're wrong, and you'd know if you let me finish.
No, no, no. Wait, please.

C1.s: A colleague asks you to check their draft to a client. It's too aggressive.
o: It's really clear. I wonder if softening the second paragraph might get a better response?
This email is rude. You can't send it.
Your email is very aggressive. The client will hate you.
n: Praise first, then a gentle suggestion.

C1.s: You're leaving the company. You tell your supportive manager.
o: I wanted you to hear it first: I've accepted another offer. I'm really grateful for your support.
I quit. My last day is the 30th.
I'm leaving because here there is no future for me.
n: Too abrupt for a good manager.
